es.R: Si alguien te pega en un lado de la cara, deja que te pegue también en el otro. Si alguien te quita el abrigo, no le impidas que se lleve también tu camisa.

sw.L: Yeye akupigaye shavuni, umgeuzie pia lile jingine; na yeye akunyang'anyaye vazi lako la nje, usimzuie kuchukua na vazi la ndani pia.
sw.B: Mtu akikupiga shavuni, mgeuzie na shavu lingine pia. Mtu akichukua koti lako, mwache achukue na shati lako pia.
sw.R: Mtu akikupiga kofi upande mmoja wa uso, mwache akupige na upande mwingine pia. Mtu akichukua koti lako, usimzuie kuchukua na shati lako.

decisions.choice: striking on the cheek: an insult as much as an injury
decisions.reason: A slap on the face was a public insult (Lamentations 3:30; Isaiah 50:6). Jesus speaks of not striking back, not of failing to protect others.

decisions.choice: cloak and tunic: the outer garment and the inner one worn next to the skin
decisions.reason: In Luke the cloak is taken first, which suggests a robbery; Matthew 5:40 speaks of a lawsuit. The tunic was the last garment a person had (3:11).

decisions.choice: do not hold back: do not refuse
alternatives: do not take back by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to hinder or keep from.

decisions.choice: coat ... shirt
decisions.reason: The nearest everyday words for the outer and inner garments, as at 3:11.

decisions.choice: te, ofrécele, déjale: "tú", with no plural_you or gender span
decisions.reason: Here and in 6:30 Jesus speaks to each hearer as one person, so Spanish uses "tú", which has no setting. The English offers "them" with "him" as the traditional form; Spanish "le" serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the gender setting to change.

decisions.choice: el manto, la túnica (L); el abrigo, la camisa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The outer garment and the one worn next to the skin (meaning decision m2). Literal names the ancient garments; Balanced and Readable use the nearest modern ones, as the English does.

decisions.choice: vazi la nje, vazi la ndani (L); koti, shati (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 5:40: the outer garment and the one worn next to the skin (meaning decision m2). Literal describes the two garments; Balanced and Readable use the nearest modern ones, as the English does.

decisions.choice: umgeuzie, mwache, usimzuie, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "them" with "him" as the traditional form. Swahili marks the person inside the verb (-m-), which serves for a man or a woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.

records.literal_gloss: To everyone asking you give, and from the one taking away the yours not ask back.

en.L: To everyone asking you, give; and from the one taking away what [is] yours, do not demand [it] back.
en.B: Keep giving to everyone who asks you for something, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not ask for it back.
en.R: Whenever someone asks you for something, give it. If someone takes things that belong to you, do not ask for them back.

es.L: A todo el que te pide, da; y al que te quita lo tuyo, no [se lo] reclames.
es.B: Da siempre a todo el que te pida algo, y si alguien te quita lo que es tuyo, no le pidas que te lo devuelva.
es.R: Cada vez que alguien te pida algo, dáselo. Si alguien se lleva cosas tuyas, no le pidas que te las devuelva.

sw.L: Kila akuombaye mpe, na yeye achukuaye vitu vyako usimdai [akurudishie].
sw.B: Endelea kumpa kila mtu anayekuomba kitu, na mtu akichukua kilicho chako, usimdai akurudishie.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akikuomba kitu, mpe. Mtu akichukua vitu vyako, usimwambie avirudishe.

decisions.choice: give ... do not demand back: present tense, what one does again and again
decisions.reason: The commands describe a way of living, not a single gift.

decisions.choice: demand back: reclaim what was taken
alternatives: ask for a loan to be repaid
decisions.reason: The verb means to ask back what is one's own.

decisions.choice: Keep giving
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the force of the present tense, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.

records.literal_gloss: And as you want that should do to you the men, do to them likewise.

en.L: And just as you want {{gender:people|men}} to do to you, do to them likewise.
en.B: However you want {{gender:people|men}} to treat you, treat them the same way.
en.R: Think about how you want others to treat you. Then treat them that way.

es.L: Y así como {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{gender:los demás|los hombres}} {{plural_you:les|os}} hagan, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} también con ellos de la misma manera.
es.B: Como {{plural_you:quieran|queráis}} que {{gender:los demás|los hombres}} {{plural_you:los|os}} traten, {{plural_you:trátenlos|tratadlos}} así a ellos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en cómo {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que los demás {{plural_you:los|os}} traten. Luego {{plural_you:trátenlos|tratadlos}} de esa manera.

sw.L: Na kama mnavyotaka watu wawatendee, watendeeni wao vivyo hivyo.
sw.B: Kama vile mnavyotaka watu wawatendee ninyi, nanyi watendeeni vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Fikirini jinsi mnavyotaka watu wengine wawatendee. Kisha nanyi watendeeni hivyo.

decisions.choice: treat others as you want to be treated: a positive command
alternatives: only a warning not to harm
decisions.reason: Jewish teaching knew the saying in a negative form: do to no one what you hate (Tobit 4:15). Jesus states it as a command to act. Matthew 7:12 adds that this sums up the Law and the Prophets.

decisions.choice: two sentences: think, then treat
decisions.reason: Readable splits the saying into two short steps.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los demás|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: Here "ellos" refers back to the people, and after "las personas" it would have to change to "ellas". "Los demás" agrees with "ellos" in both wordings, so only the noun phrase changes.

source.text: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you love those loving you, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you love those loving you, what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: If you love those who love you, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you love only the people who love you, should anyone thank you for that?

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:aman|amáis}} a los que {{plural_you:los|os}} aman, ¿qué clase de reconocimiento es [ese] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Si {{plural_you:aman|amáis}} a quienes {{plural_you:los|os}} aman, ¿qué agradecimiento {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}}?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:aman|amáis}} solo a los que {{plural_you:los|os}} aman, ¿por qué alguien tendría que {{plural_you:darles|daros}} las gracias?

sw.L: Na kama mnawapenda wale wanaowapenda, ni shukrani ya namna gani kwenu?
sw.B: Mkiwapenda wale wanaowapenda, mnastahili shukrani gani?
sw.R: Mkiwapenda tu watu wanaowapenda, je, kuna mtu anayepaswa kuwashukuru kwa hilo?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: The word usually translated "grace" here means credit or thanks. The question asks what is so special about such love. Matthew 5:46 has "what reward"; some read the thanks as God's favor (compare 6:35).

decisions.choice: what kind of: a question expecting the answer none
alternatives: a real question about how much credit
decisions.reason: The question says that such love deserves no special thanks.

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "grace" would mislead here, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: only
decisions.reason: Readable makes the contrast clear: love that goes only to those who love back.

decisions.choice: reconocimiento (L); agradecimiento (B); dar las gracias (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one usually rendered "gracia", but here it means the thanks or credit an act deserves (meaning decision m1), so the key term is not used. The same in 6:33 and 6:34.

decisions.choice: shukrani (L, B); kuwashukuru (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one rendered "neema" elsewhere, but here it means the thanks or credit an act deserves (meaning decision m1), so the key term is not used. The same in 6:33 and 6:34.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Even for the sinners those loving them love.

en.L: For even the sinners love those loving them.
en.B: After all, sinners too love those who love them back.
en.R: Even sinful people love those who love them.

es.L: Porque también los pecadores aman a los que los aman.
es.B: Al fin y al cabo, también los pecadores aman a quienes los aman a ellos.
es.R: Hasta los pecadores aman a los que los aman.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata wenye dhambi huwapenda wale wanaowapenda.
sw.B: Hata wenye dhambi huwapenda wale wanaowapenda.
sw.R: Hata watu wenye dhambi huwapenda wale wanaowapenda.

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for not keeping God's law
decisions.reason: In the Gospels "sinners" are people who openly ignore God's law, often named with tax collectors (5:30). Matthew 5:46 has "tax collectors" here.

decisions.choice: sinful people
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you do good to those doing good to you, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you do good to those doing good to you, what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you do good things only for people who do good things for you, should anyone thank you for that?

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien a los que {{plural_you:les|os}} hacen el bien, ¿qué clase de reconocimiento es [ese] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Y si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} el bien a quienes {{plural_you:les|os}} hacen el bien, ¿qué agradecimiento {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}}?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} cosas buenas solo por los que {{plural_you:les|os}} hacen cosas buenas, ¿por qué alguien tendría que {{plural_you:darles|daros}} las gracias?

sw.L: Na kama mnawatendea mema wale wanaowatendea mema, ni shukrani ya namna gani kwenu?
sw.B: Na mkiwatendea mema wale wanaowatendea mema, mnastahili shukrani gani?
sw.R: Mkiwatendea mambo mazuri wale tu wanaowatendea mambo mazuri, je, kuna mtu anayepaswa kuwashukuru kwa hilo?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: As in 6:32, the word usually translated "grace" means credit or thanks.

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:32.

source.text: καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Even the sinners the same do.

en.L: Even the sinners do the same.
en.B: Even sinners do as much.
en.R: Sinful people do that too.

es.L: También los pecadores hacen lo mismo.
es.B: Hasta los pecadores hacen otro tanto.
es.R: Los pecadores también hacen eso.

sw.L: Hata wenye dhambi hufanya vivyo hivyo.
sw.B: Hata wenye dhambi hufanya hivyo.
sw.R: Watu wenye dhambi nao hufanya hivyo.

decisions.choice: even: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: for even, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "for", as in 6:32. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ’ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν;

records.literal_gloss: And if you lend [to those] from whom you hope to receive, what kind of to you credit is it?

en.L: And if you lend [to those] from whom you hope to receive [back], what kind of credit is [it] to you?
en.B: And if you lend to people you expect to pay you back, what thanks do you deserve?
en.R: If you lend money only to people who you think will pay you back, should anyone thank you for that?

es.L: Y si {{plural_you:prestan|prestáis}} [a aquellos] de quienes {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}} recibir [de vuelta], ¿qué clase de reconocimiento es [ese] para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}?
es.B: Y si {{plural_you:prestan|prestáis}} a quienes {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} paguen, ¿qué agradecimiento {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}}?
es.R: Si {{plural_you:prestan|prestáis}} dinero solo a los que {{plural_you:creen|creéis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} van a pagar, ¿por qué alguien tendría que {{plural_you:darles|daros}} las gracias?

sw.L: Na kama mnawakopesha wale ambao mnatumaini kupokea [kitu] kutoka kwao, ni shukrani ya namna gani kwenu?
sw.B: Na mkiwakopesha watu mnaotarajia watawalipa, mnastahili shukrani gani?
sw.R: Mkiwakopesha pesa wale tu mnaodhani watawalipa, je, kuna mtu anayepaswa kuwashukuru kwa hilo?

decisions.choice: credit: thanks, the favor earned by an act that deserves it
decisions.reason: As in 6:32, the word usually translated "grace" means credit or thanks.

decisions.choice: lend: lending to a neighbor in need
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to lend freely to a poor neighbor and not to charge interest (Deuteronomy 15:7-8; Leviticus 25:35-37).

decisions.choice: credit (L); thanks (B); thank you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:32.

decisions.choice: money
decisions.reason: Readable says what is lent.

source.text: καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.

records.literal_gloss: Even sinners to sinners lend so that they might receive back the equal [things].

en.L: Even sinners lend to sinners so that they may receive back the same [amount].
en.B: Sinners also lend to sinners, so as to get back as much again.
en.R: Even sinful people lend to other sinful people, so that they will get back the same amount.

es.L: También los pecadores prestan a los pecadores para recibir de vuelta otro tanto.
es.B: También los pecadores prestan a otros pecadores para que se les devuelva otro tanto.
es.R: Hasta los pecadores les prestan a otros pecadores para que les devuelvan la misma cantidad.

sw.L: Hata wenye dhambi huwakopesha wenye dhambi ili warudishiwe kiasi kile kile.
sw.B: Hata wenye dhambi huwakopesha wenye dhambi wenzao ili walipwe kiasi kile kile.
sw.R: Hata watu wenye dhambi huwakopesha wenye dhambi wengine ili warudishiwe kiasi kile kile.

decisions.choice: the same: the same amount as was lent
alternatives: a like favor in return, a loan when they need one
decisions.reason: The words mean "the equal things". Either way, the lender looks for a return.

source.text: πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες· καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.

records.literal_gloss: But love the enemies of you and do good and lend nothing expecting in return; and will be the reward of you great, and you will be sons of [the] Most High, for he kind is to the ungrateful and evil.

en.L: Rather, love your enemies and do good and lend, hoping for nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of [the] Most High, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is kind toward the ungrateful and evil [ones].
en.B: Instead, love your enemies, treat them well, and lend without hoping to get anything back. Then you will receive a great reward, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of the Most High, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good to the thankless and the wicked.
en.R: Instead, love your enemies. Do good to them. Lend to them, and do not expect to get anything back. Then you will have a great reward, and you will be {{gender:children|sons}} of God Most High. For God is kind to people who never thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to people who are evil.

es.L: Al contrario, {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos, y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} el bien, y {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} sin esperar nada a cambio; y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} recompensa será grande, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} hijos del Altísimo, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es bondadoso con los ingratos y malvados.
es.B: Más bien, {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos, {{plural_you:trátenlos|tratadlos}} bien y {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} sin esperar nada a cambio. Así {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} una gran recompensa y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} hijos del Altísimo, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es bueno con los desagradecidos y con los malvados.
es.R: Al contrario, {{plural_you:amen|amad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} enemigos. {{plural_you:Háganles|Hacedles}} el bien. {{plural_you:Préstenles|Prestadles}}, y no {{plural_you:esperen|esperéis}} recibir nada a cambio. Entonces {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} una gran recompensa, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} hijos del Dios Altísimo. Porque Dios es bueno con los que nunca {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dan las gracias y con los malvados.

sw.L: Bali wapendeni maadui wenu, na tendeni mema, na kopesheni bila kutumaini kurudishiwa chochote; na ujira wenu utakuwa mkubwa, nanyi mtakuwa wana wa Aliye Juu Kabisa, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwema kwa wasio na shukrani na waovu.
sw.B: Badala yake, wapendeni maadui wenu, watendeeni mema, na mkopeshe bila kutarajia kurudishiwa chochote. Ndipo mtapata ujira mkubwa, nanyi mtakuwa wana wa Aliye Juu Kabisa, kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwema kwa wasio na shukrani na kwa waovu.
sw.R: Badala yake, wapendeni maadui wenu. Watendeeni mema. Wakopesheni, wala msitarajie kurudishiwa chochote. Ndipo mtakuwa na ujira mkubwa, nanyi mtakuwa wana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa. Kwa maana Mungu ni mwema kwa watu wasiomshukuru kamwe, na kwa watu waovu.

decisions.choice: hoping for nothing back: expecting no return
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to give up hope. Here, after "lend" and set against 6:34, it means to hope for something in return.

decisions.choice: nothing: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no one, the reading of a few early manuscripts, giving "despairing of no one"
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have a form meaning "no one", which gives the sense "giving up on no one". Most have "nothing". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: children of the Most High: people who share God's character
alternatives: a title earned by good works
decisions.reason: Children take after their father. Those who love their enemies act as God acts. "The Most High" is a name for God (1:32, 35; Genesis 14:18-20). The word is "sons", but the saying is for all who listen.

decisions.choice: kind: good, generous
decisions.reason: The word describes goodness that gives to those who do not deserve it.

decisions.choice: rather: a strong contrast with 6:32-34
decisions.reason: Jesus sets his command against the way sinners love, do good and lend.

decisions.choice: treat them well (B); Do good to them (R)
decisions.reason: The context shows that the enemies are the ones to whom good is done.

decisions.choice: God Most High
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "the Most High" is God, as at 1:35.

decisions.choice: hijos, with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 5:45: Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters, so the English "children|sons" setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: el Altísimo (L, B); el Dios Altísimo (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for this name of God; Readable adds "Dios", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wana, with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 5:45: "wana" is used of sons and daughters alike, so the English "children|sons" setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: Aliye Juu Kabisa (L, B); Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for this name of God; Readable adds "Mungu", as the English Readable does.

source.text: γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν·

records.literal_gloss: Become compassionate as the Father of you compassionate is.

en.L: Become compassionate, as your Father is compassionate.
en.B: Show compassion, as your Father shows compassion.
en.R: Have compassion for others, just as your Father has compassion.

es.L: {{plural_you:Lleguen|Llegad}} a ser compasivos, como {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre es compasivo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Muestren|Mostrad}} compasión, como {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre muestra compasión.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} compasión de los demás, así como {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre tiene compasión.

sw.L: Kuweni wenye huruma, kama Baba yenu alivyo mwenye huruma.
sw.B: Onyesheni huruma, kama Baba yenu anavyoonyesha huruma.
sw.R: Wahurumieni wengine, kama vile Baba yenu anavyowahurumia watu.

decisions.choice: compassionate: feeling pity and acting on it
decisions.reason: The word is not the usual one for mercy. It is used of God in the Greek Old Testament of Exodus 34:6 and Psalm 103:8 (102:8 in that numbering): the LORD is compassionate and gracious.

decisions.choice: become: a call to grow into this likeness
alternatives: be, as a state already reached
decisions.reason: The verb means to become; the present tense shows a way of life.

decisions.choice: your Father: God, the Father of those who belong to him
decisions.reason: This picks up "children of the Most High" in 6:35.

decisions.choice: compassionate (L); show compassion (B); have compassion (R)
decisions.reason: The usual word is "merciful", but the Greek word stresses pity that moves to help.

source.text: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε· καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε.

records.literal_gloss: And not judge, and not not you will be judged; and not condemn, and not not you will be condemned.

en.L: And do not judge, and you will certainly not be judged; and do not condemn, and you will certainly not be condemned.
en.B: Do not sit in judgment on others, and you will never be judged. Do not pass sentence on them, and no sentence will be passed on you.
en.R: Do not judge other people, and God will not judge you. Do not say that others are guilty, and God will not say that you are guilty.

es.L: Y no {{plural_you:juzguen|juzguéis}}, y de ningún modo {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados; y no {{plural_you:condenen|condenéis}}, y de ningún modo {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} condenados.
es.B: No {{plural_you:se pongan|os pongáis}} a juzgar a los demás, y jamás {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados. No {{plural_you:dicten|dictéis}} sentencia contra ellos, y no se dictará sentencia contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: No {{plural_you:juzguen|juzguéis}} a otras personas, y Dios no {{plural_you:los|os}} juzgará. No {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} que otros son culpables, y Dios no dirá que {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} culpables.

sw.L: Na msihukumu, na hakika hamtahukumiwa; na msiwatie [watu] hatiani, na hakika hamtatiwa hatiani.
sw.B: Msiwe watu wa kuwahukumu wengine, nanyi hamtahukumiwa kamwe. Msiwatie wengine hatiani, nanyi hamtatiwa hatiani.
sw.R: Msiwahukumu watu wengine, naye Mungu hatawahukumu. Msiseme kwamba wengine wana hatia, naye Mungu hatasema kwamba ninyi mna hatia.

decisions.choice: judge: pass judgment on others, find fault
decisions.reason: Jesus forbids setting oneself up as judge over others. He still asks his hearers to tell good fruit from bad (6:43-45).

decisions.choice: you will certainly not be judged: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two negatives together for emphasis.

decisions.choice: be judged, be condemned: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God unnamed, as in 6:21 and 6:38.

decisions.choice: sit in judgment ... pass sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the picture of a judge in court.

decisions.choice: God will not judge you ... God will not say
alternatives: you will not be judged ... condemned
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἀπολύετε, καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε·

records.literal_gloss: Release, and you will be released;

en.L: Release, and you will be released.
en.B: Pardon others, and you will be pardoned.
en.R: Forgive others, and God will forgive you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Liberen|Liberad}}, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} liberados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Absuelvan|Absolved}} a los demás, y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} absueltos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Perdonen|Perdonad}} a los demás, y Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} perdonará.

sw.L: Achilieni, nanyi mtaachiliwa.
sw.B: Wasameheni wengine makosa yao, nanyi mtasamehewa.
sw.R: Wasameheni wengine, naye Mungu atawasamehe.

decisions.choice: release: pardon, set free from a debt or a wrong
decisions.reason: The verb means to let go. Beside "judge" and "condemn" it means to release someone from the charge, that is, to forgive.

decisions.choice: pardon (B); forgive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the release means here.

decisions.choice: God will forgive you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as in 6:37.

decisions.choice: liberar (L); absolver (B); perdonar (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is to release, set free from a debt or a wrong (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the picture; Balanced says "absolver", the word for pardoning someone charged, as the English says "pardon".

decisions.choice: achilieni ... mtaachiliwa (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek is to release, set free from a debt or a wrong (meaning decision m1). "Kuachilia" keeps that picture at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "kusamehe", the everyday word for pardon.

source.text: δίδοτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν· ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Give, and it will be given to you; measure good, pressed down, shaken together, running over they will give into the lap of you; with which for measure you measure it will be measured back to you.

en.L: Give, and it will be given to you; a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, overflowing, they will give into your lap; for with the measure with which you measure, it will be measured back to you."
en.B: Give, and gifts will come to you: a full measure, packed down, shaken to settle it, and spilling over the top, will be poured into the fold of your robe. The measure you use for others is the measure that will be used for you."
en.R: Give to others, and you will be given much. It will be poured into the fold of your robe like grain in a full measure. It will be pressed down and shaken to make room for more, until it spills over. The way you measure out to others is the way God will measure out to you."

es.L: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}}, y se {{plural_you:les|os}} dará; una medida buena, apretada, sacudida y desbordante {{plural_you:les|os}} darán en el regazo; porque con la medida con que {{plural_you:miden|medís}} se {{plural_you:les|os}} medirá de vuelta».
es.B: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}}, y {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}}: una medida llena, bien apretada, sacudida para que se asiente y desbordándose por encima, se derramará en el pliegue de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} manto. La medida que {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} con los demás es la que se usará con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.R: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} a los demás, y {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} mucho. Se {{plural_you:les|os}} echará en el pliegue del manto, como grano en una medida llena. Estará apretado y sacudido para que quepa más, hasta que se desborde. Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dará con la misma medida que {{plural_you:usen|uséis}} con los demás».

sw.L: Toeni, nanyi mtapewa; kipimo kizuri, kilichoshindiliwa, kilichotikiswa, kinachofurika, watawapa mapajani mwenu; kwa maana kwa kipimo kile mnachopimia, mtapimiwa kwacho."
sw.B: Toeni, nanyi mtapewa: kipimo kilichojaa, kilichoshindiliwa, kilichotikiswa kikatulia, na kinachomwagika juu, kitamiminwa katika kunjo la vazi lenu. Kipimo mnachotumia kwa wengine ndicho kitakachotumiwa kwenu."
sw.R: Wapeni wengine, nanyi mtapewa mengi. Mtamiminiwa katika kunjo la nguo zenu kama nafaka katika kipimo kilichojaa. Kitashindiliwa na kutikiswa ili kipate nafasi zaidi, mpaka kimwagike. Jinsi mnavyowapimia wengine, ndivyo Mungu atakavyowapimia ninyi."

decisions.choice: a good measure, pressed down, shaken, overflowing: a picture from the grain market
decisions.reason: A generous seller filled the measuring vessel, pressed the grain down and shook it to settle it, then filled it again until it ran over. The buyer carried it away in the fold of the robe above the belt, used as a pocket (compare Ruth 3:15). The measure is a picture, not a fixed amount.

decisions.choice: they will give: an indefinite "they", a way of speaking of God's action
decisions.reason: Jewish speech often avoided naming God. The rest of the verse speaks of God's giving, though people may be the means of it.

decisions.choice: the measure you use will be measured back: as you treat others, so God will treat you
decisions.reason: The saying was proverbial (compare Mark 4:24). Here it sums up 6:37-38.

decisions.choice: the fold of your robe
decisions.reason: The "lap" here is the fold of the garment used for carrying things.

decisions.choice: God will measure out to you
alternatives: it will be measured back to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here and opens again in 6:39
decisions.reason: The narrator's words in 6:39 break into the speech.

decisions.choice: el regazo (L); el pliegue del manto (B, R)
decisions.reason: The picture is grain poured into the fold of a robe gathered above the belt, used as a pocket (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "regazo"; Balanced and Readable say where the grain goes, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mapajani (L); kunjo la vazi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The picture is grain poured into the fold of a robe gathered above the belt, used as a pocket (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "lap"; Balanced and Readable say where the grain goes, as the English does.

source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: He spoke then also a parable to them; Not is able blind blind to lead?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also told them a parable: "Is a blind [person] able to guide a blind [person]?
en.B: He also told them a parable: "Can one blind person be a guide to another?
en.R: Jesus also used a picture to teach them: "Can a blind person lead another blind person?

es.L: Y les dijo también una parábola: «¿Acaso puede un ciego guiar a [otro] ciego?
es.B: También les contó una parábola: «¿Puede un ciego servir de guía a otro ciego?
es.R: Jesús también les enseñó con una comparación: «¿Puede un ciego guiar a otro ciego?

sw.L: Akawaambia pia mfano: "Je, kipofu aweza kumwongoza kipofu?
sw.B: Pia aliwaambia mfano: "Je, kipofu anaweza kuwa kiongozi wa kipofu mwenzake?
sw.R: Yesu pia aliwafundisha kwa mfano: "Je, kipofu anaweza kumwongoza kipofu mwingine?

decisions.choice: parable: a comparison or picture-saying
decisions.reason: The word can mean a short saying that makes a comparison, as in 4:23 and 5:36. 6:39-45 is a series of such pictures.

decisions.choice: is a blind person able: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The Greek word marks the question as one that expects no.

decisions.choice: a blind guide: a teacher who does not see cannot lead others
decisions.reason: The saying warns those who will teach (6:40) and those who follow them. Matthew 15:14 uses it of the Pharisees.

decisions.choice: used a picture to teach them
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of parable this is: a picture, not a story.

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); les enseñó con una comparación (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts; here the parable is a short picture-saying (meaning decision m1), so Readable follows the English Readable's "used a picture to teach them".

source.text: οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ἐμπεσοῦνται;

records.literal_gloss: Not both into a pit will fall?

en.L: Will not both fall into a pit?
en.B: Both of them will end up in a ditch, will they not?
en.R: Both of them will fall into a hole, will they not?

es.L: ¿No caerán ambos en un hoyo?
es.B: Los dos terminarán en una zanja, ¿no es así?
es.R: Los dos se caerán en un hoyo, ¿no es cierto?

sw.L: Je, wote wawili hawatatumbukia shimoni?
sw.B: Wote wawili wataishia shimoni, sivyo?
sw.R: Wote wawili wataanguka ndani ya shimo, sivyo?

decisions.choice: pit: a hole or ditch dug in the ground
decisions.reason: Open pits, cisterns and ditches were a real danger to anyone walking without sight.

decisions.choice: will not both fall: a question expecting the answer yes
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects yes.

source.text: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον, κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not is a disciple above the teacher, fully trained but everyone will be like the teacher of him.

en.L: A disciple is not above the teacher, but everyone, having been fully trained, will be like {{gender:their|his}} teacher.
en.B: No disciple ranks above the teacher, but every disciple who is fully trained will become like the teacher.
en.R: A student is not greater than the teacher. But when students have learned everything, they will be like their teacher.

es.L: Un discípulo no está por encima del maestro, pero todo [el que haya sido] plenamente formado será como su maestro.
es.B: Ningún discípulo está por encima del maestro, pero todo discípulo bien formado llegará a ser como su maestro.
es.R: Un alumno no es más importante que su maestro. Pero cuando los alumnos han aprendido todo, llegan a ser como su maestro.

sw.L: Mwanafunzi hayuko juu ya mwalimu, lakini kila aliyefundishwa kikamilifu atakuwa kama mwalimu wake.
sw.B: Hakuna mwanafunzi aliye juu ya mwalimu, lakini kila mwanafunzi aliyefundishwa kikamilifu atakuwa kama mwalimu wake.
sw.R: Mwanafunzi si mkubwa kuliko mwalimu wake. Lakini wanafunzi wakishajifunza kila kitu, watakuwa kama mwalimu wao.

decisions.choice: fully trained: made complete, fully equipped
decisions.reason: The verb is used of mending nets (Mark 1:19) and of making complete.

decisions.choice: a disciple becomes like the teacher: so the teacher must see clearly
alternatives: a promise that disciples will surpass their teacher
decisions.reason: After the blind guide (6:39), the point is that followers can rise no higher than their teacher. Who one follows matters.

decisions.choice: student
decisions.reason: In this saying the word has its everyday sense of one who learns from a teacher.

decisions.choice: alumno (R)
decisions.reason: A general saying about any teacher and pupil, where the English Readable says "student". The term sheet keeps "discípulos" for Jesus's disciples at every level; here no particular disciples are meant, and "alumno" is the plain word.

decisions.choice: su maestro, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "su" serves for "his" or "their", so the English "their|his" setting has nothing to change.

source.text: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: Why then do you see the splinter in the eye of the brother of you, the but beam in the own eye not you notice?

en.L: And why do you look at the splinter that [is] in the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, but the beam that [is] in your own eye you do not notice?
en.B: Why do you stare at the splinter in the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, and fail to notice the wooden beam in your own?
en.R: Why do you notice a tiny speck in the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, but you do not see the big piece of wood in your own eye?

es.L: ¿Y por qué ves la brizna que [hay] en el ojo de tu hermano, pero no reparas en la viga que [hay] en tu propio ojo?
es.B: ¿Por qué te fijas en la mota que tiene tu hermano en el ojo, y no te das cuenta de la viga que tienes en el tuyo?
es.R: ¿Por qué ves una mota pequeñita en el ojo de tu hermano, pero no ves el gran pedazo de madera que tienes en tu propio ojo?

sw.L: Na kwa nini unakitazama kibanzi kilicho katika jicho la ndugu yako, lakini gogo lililo katika jicho lako mwenyewe hulitambui?
sw.B: Kwa nini unakikodolea macho kibanzi kilicho katika jicho la ndugu yako, wala huoni gogo lililo katika jicho lako mwenyewe?
sw.R: Kwa nini unaona takataka ndogo sana katika jicho la ndugu yako, lakini huoni kipande kikubwa cha mti katika jicho lako mwenyewe?

decisions.choice: splinter ... beam: a tiny chip of wood or straw, and a large timber
decisions.reason: The first word means a small dry stalk or chip; the second, a main beam of a house.

decisions.choice: a splinter in another's eye, a beam in one's own: noticing small faults in others while blind to one's own great ones
decisions.reason: The picture is deliberately absurd, to make the point stick.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is used of anyone who belongs to the same community (17:3).

decisions.choice: splinter ... beam (L, B); tiny speck ... big piece of wood (R)
decisions.reason: The words picture a chip of wood beside a timber. Readable describes them in plain words.

decisions.choice: tu hermano, with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 7:3: "hermano" in a saying like this covers any fellow member of God's people, man or woman (meaning decision m3), so there is no span here or in 6:42, where the English has one.

decisions.choice: brizna (L), mota (B, R); viga (L, B), gran pedazo de madera (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 7:3: the smallest thing that can get into an eye against a roof beam (meaning decision m1), keeping the absurd contrast. The same in 6:42.

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means a brother or a sister (meaning decision m3), so Swahili needs no gender span here or in 6:42, where the English has one.

decisions.choice: kibanzi (splinter); gogo (log)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 7:3: a tiny fault set against a huge one (meaning decision m1). "Gogo", a whole log, makes the absurd size plain; "boriti" is a building beam. The same in 6:42.

source.text: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων;

records.literal_gloss: How are you able to say to the brother of you, Brother, allow, I may cast out the splinter in the eye of you, yourself the in the eye of you beam not seeing?

en.L: How are you able to say to your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, '{{gender:Brother or sister|Brother}}, allow [me], let me cast out the splinter that [is] in your eye,' while you yourself do not see the beam in your [own] eye?
en.B: How can you tell your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, '{{gender:Brother or sister|Brother}}, here, let me get that splinter out of your eye,' when you cannot see the beam in your own eye?
en.R: How can you say to your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, '{{gender:Brother or sister|Brother}}, let me take that speck out of your eye,' when you cannot see the big piece of wood in your own eye?

es.L: ¿Cómo puedes decir a tu hermano: “Hermano, deja que saque la brizna que [hay] en tu ojo”, no viendo tú mismo la viga que [hay] en tu ojo?
es.B: ¿Cómo puedes decirle a tu hermano: “Hermano, a ver, déjame sacarte esa mota del ojo”, cuando no ves la viga que tienes en el tuyo?
es.R: ¿Cómo puedes decirle a tu hermano: “Hermano, déjame quitarte esa mota del ojo”, si no puedes ver el gran pedazo de madera que tienes en tu propio ojo?

sw.L: Unawezaje kumwambia ndugu yako, 'Ndugu, niache nikitoe kibanzi kilicho katika jicho lako,' wakati wewe mwenyewe huoni gogo lililo katika jicho lako?
sw.B: Unawezaje kumwambia ndugu yako, 'Ndugu yangu, hebu nikutoe kibanzi hicho jichoni,' wakati huwezi kuliona gogo lililo katika jicho lako mwenyewe?
sw.R: Unawezaje kumwambia ndugu yako, 'Ndugu yangu, acha nikutoe takataka hiyo jichoni,' wakati huwezi kuona kipande kikubwa cha mti kilicho katika jicho lako mwenyewe?

decisions.choice: allow, let me cast out: a polite offer
decisions.reason: The words are a friendly request, which makes the picture more absurd.

decisions.choice: you yourself not seeing: the one who offers help is blind to a greater fault
decisions.reason: The picture of 6:41 is carried on.

source.text: ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Hypocrite, cast out first the beam from the eye of you, and then you will see clearly the splinter in the eye of the brother of you to cast out.

en.L: Hypocrite, cast out first the beam from your eye, and then you will see clearly to cast out the splinter that [is] in the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}.
en.B: You hypocrite! Get the beam out of your own eye first. Then you will see well enough to remove the splinter from the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}.
en.R: You hypocrite! First take the big piece of wood out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly enough to take the speck out of the eye of your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}.

es.L: Hipócrita, saca primero la viga de tu ojo, y entonces verás con claridad para sacar la brizna que [hay] en el ojo de tu hermano.
es.B: ¡Hipócrita! Primero saca la viga de tu propio ojo. Entonces verás lo bastante bien para quitar la mota del ojo de tu hermano.
es.R: ¡Hipócrita! Primero saca de tu propio ojo el gran pedazo de madera. Entonces verás con claridad para sacar la mota del ojo de tu hermano.

sw.L: Mnafiki, toa kwanza gogo katika jicho lako, na ndipo utaona vizuri kukitoa kibanzi kilicho katika jicho la ndugu yako.
sw.B: Wewe mnafiki! Kwanza ondoa gogo katika jicho lako mwenyewe. Ndipo utaona vizuri vya kutosha kukiondoa kibanzi katika jicho la ndugu yako.
sw.R: Wewe mnafiki! Kwanza toa kipande kikubwa cha mti katika jicho lako mwenyewe. Ndipo utaona vizuri, uweze kutoa takataka katika jicho la ndugu yako.

decisions.choice: hypocrite: one who plays a part, whose show of goodness does not match the reality
decisions.reason: The word first meant an actor on a stage. Jesus uses it of people who look at others' faults and hide their own (12:56; 13:15).

decisions.choice: then you will see clearly: correcting others is not forbidden, but it must come after dealing with oneself
decisions.reason: Jesus still expects the splinter to be taken out.

source.text: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.

records.literal_gloss: Not for is tree good producing fruit bad, nor again tree bad producing fruit good.

en.L: For there is no good tree producing bad fruit, nor again a bad tree producing good fruit.
en.B: For a sound tree does not yield rotten fruit, and a rotten tree does not yield sound fruit either.
en.R: A good tree does not grow bad fruit. A bad tree does not grow good fruit either.

es.L: Porque no hay árbol bueno que produzca fruto podrido, ni a su vez árbol podrido que produzca fruto bueno.
es.B: Porque un árbol sano no da fruto podrido, ni tampoco un árbol podrido da fruto sano.
es.R: Un árbol bueno no da fruta mala. Y un árbol malo tampoco da fruta buena.

sw.L: Kwa maana hakuna mti mzuri uzaao matunda mabovu, wala tena mti mbovu uzaao matunda mazuri.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa mti wenye afya hauzai matunda mabovu, wala mti mbovu hauzai matunda mazuri.
sw.R: Mti mzuri hauzai matunda mabaya. Wala mti mbaya hauzai matunda mazuri.

decisions.choice: good ... bad: healthy and diseased, sound and rotten
alternatives: morally good and evil, with no picture
decisions.reason: The words describe the condition of the tree and its fruit. The second means rotten or worthless.

decisions.choice: for: what a person is inside shows in what they produce
alternatives: no link with what goes before
decisions.reason: The saying gives the reason behind 6:41-42: a heart that is not right cannot bring out good (6:45).

decisions.choice: sound ... rotten
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of a tree's health.

source.text: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Each for tree by the own fruit is known; not for from thorns do they gather figs, nor from a bramble bush grapes do they pick.

en.L: For each tree is known by its own fruit; for not from thorns do they gather figs, nor from a bramble bush do they harvest grapes.
en.B: You can tell every tree by its own fruit. No one gathers figs from thorn plants or picks grapes off a bramble bush.
en.R: You can tell what kind of tree it is by looking at its fruit. People do not pick figs from thorny weeds. They do not pick grapes from bushes full of thorns.

es.L: Pues cada árbol se conoce por su propio fruto; porque no se recogen higos de los espinos, ni se vendimian uvas de una zarza.
es.B: Cada árbol se reconoce por su fruto. Nadie recoge higos de los espinos ni corta uvas de una zarza.
es.R: Por la fruta se sabe qué clase de árbol es. La gente no recoge higos de las hierbas espinosas. Tampoco recoge uvas de los arbustos llenos de espinas.

sw.L: Kwa maana kila mti hujulikana kwa matunda yake wenyewe; kwa sababu hawachumi tini kwenye miiba, wala hawavuni zabibu kwenye kichaka cha michongoma.
sw.B: Kila mti hutambulika kwa matunda yake. Watu hawachumi tini kwenye miiba, wala hawachumi zabibu kwenye michongoma.
sw.R: Unaweza kujua mti ni wa aina gani kwa kuangalia matunda yake. Watu hawachumi tini kwenye magugu yenye miiba. Hawachumi zabibu kwenye vichaka vilivyojaa miiba.

decisions.choice: known by its fruit: a person is known by what they say and do
decisions.reason: Fruit is what a life produces (3:8-9). 6:45 applies the picture to speech.

decisions.choice: thorns, bramble bush: wild plants with no useful fruit
decisions.reason: Thorns and brambles grew among the fields and vineyards and were cleared away and burned.

source.text: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν· ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The good man out of the good treasure of the heart of him brings forth the good, and the evil out of the evil brings forth the evil; out of for abundance of heart speaks the mouth of him.

en.L: The good {{gender:person|man}} out of the good treasure of {{gender:their|his}} heart brings forth what is good, and the evil [one] out of the evil [treasure] brings forth what is evil; for out of [the] abundance of [the] heart {{gender:their|his}} mouth speaks.
en.B: From the good treasure in {{gender:their|his}} heart, a good {{gender:person|man}} produces what is good, and from what is evil, an evil {{gender:person|man}} produces what is evil. For the mouth speaks out of what overflows the heart.
en.R: Good people have good things saved up inside them, like treasure in their hearts, and good things come out of them. Evil people have evil inside them, and evil things come out. What people say shows what fills their hearts.

es.L: {{gender:La persona buena|El hombre bueno}}, del buen tesoro de su corazón, saca lo bueno, y el malo, del mal [tesoro], saca lo malo; porque de [la] abundancia [del] corazón habla su boca.
es.B: Del buen tesoro que hay en su corazón, {{gender:una persona buena|un hombre bueno}} saca lo que es bueno; y de lo que es malo, {{gender:una persona mala|un hombre malo}} saca lo que es malo. Porque la boca habla de lo que desborda el corazón.
es.R: Las personas buenas tienen cosas buenas guardadas dentro, como un tesoro en el corazón, y de ellas salen cosas buenas. Las personas malas tienen maldad dentro, y de ellas salen cosas malas. Lo que la gente dice muestra lo que llena su corazón.

sw.L: Mtu mwema, kutoka katika hazina njema ya moyo wake, hutoa yaliyo mema; na mwovu, kutoka katika [hazina] iliyo ovu, hutoa yaliyo maovu; kwa maana kutoka katika wingi wa moyo kinywa chake hunena.
sw.B: Mtu mwema hutoa yaliyo mema kutoka katika hazina njema ya moyo wake, na mtu mwovu hutoa yaliyo maovu kutoka katika yaliyo maovu. Kwa maana kinywa hunena yale yanayoujaza moyo hadi kufurika.
sw.R: Watu wema wana mambo mema yaliyohifadhiwa ndani yao, kama hazina mioyoni mwao, na mambo mema hutoka ndani yao. Watu waovu wana uovu ndani yao, na mambo maovu hutoka. Maneno ya watu huonyesha kile kinachojaza mioyo yao.

decisions.choice: the treasure of the heart: what is stored up within a person
decisions.reason: A treasure is a storeroom. What is kept inside comes out in time.

decisions.choice: heart: the inner self, where a person thinks and decides
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is the center of thought and will (2:19, 35).

decisions.choice: the evil out of the evil: "person" and "treasure" understood
alternatives: evil things out of evil things
decisions.reason: The second half is shortened; the words are supplied from the first half.

decisions.choice: abundance: what fills to overflowing
decisions.reason: What a person says spills out of what fills the heart.

decisions.choice: good people ... evil people ... what people say
alternatives: the good person ... the evil person ... his mouth
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of people in general, which is what the saying means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:La persona buena|El hombre bueno}}; "su corazón", "su boca" plain
decisions.reason: The English has spans on "person|man" and "their|his". Spanish "su" already serves for either, so only the noun phrase changes; at Literal "el malo" (the evil one) is the ordinary form for anyone and stays plain.

source.text: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε· Κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;

records.literal_gloss: Why then me do you call, Lord, Lord, and not do what I say?

en.L: And why do you call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Lord, Lord,' and you do not do the things I say?
en.B: Why do you keep calling {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'Lord, Lord' when you do not do what I tell you?
en.R: You call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} 'Lord, Lord!' So why do you not do what I tell you?

es.L: ¿Y por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}}: “Señor, Señor”, y no {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que digo?
es.B: ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:siguen|seguís}} llamando “Señor, Señor”, si no {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo?
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}}: “¡Señor, Señor!”. Entonces, ¿por qué no {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} digo?

sw.L: Na kwa nini mnaniita, 'Bwana, Bwana,' na hamfanyi ninayosema?
sw.B: Kwa nini mnaendelea kuniita 'Bwana, Bwana,' wakati hamfanyi ninayowaambia?
sw.R: Mnaniita, 'Bwana, Bwana!' Basi kwa nini hamfanyi ninayowaambia?

decisions.choice: Lord: master, the one whose authority is confessed
decisions.reason: The word can be polite, but repeated it is earnest, the address of those who claim to follow him. Jesus asks why their deeds do not match it.

decisions.choice: you call: you keep calling
decisions.reason: The present tense describes a habit.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks around "Lord, Lord"
decisions.reason: The words are quoted inside Jesus's speech.

source.text: πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος·

records.literal_gloss: Everyone coming to me and hearing of me the words and doing them, I will show you whom he is like;

en.L: Everyone who comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and does them, I will show you whom {{gender:they are|he is}} like:
en.B: Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} show you what someone is like who comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, listens to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, and acts on them.
en.R: Let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} show you what a person is like who comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, listens to what I say, and obeys it.

es.L: Todo el que viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y oye {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y las hace, {{plural_you:les|os}} mostraré a quién es semejante:
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} voy a mostrar a quién se parece el que viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, escucha {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y las pone en práctica.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} voy a mostrar cómo es la persona que viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, escucha lo que digo y lo obedece.

sw.L: Kila mtu ajaye {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} na kuyasikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuyatenda, nitawaonyesha anafanana na nani:
sw.B: Nitawaonyesha jinsi alivyo mtu anayekuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anayesikiliza maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuyatekeleza.
sw.R: Nitawaonyesha jinsi alivyo mtu anayekuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, anayesikiliza ninayosema na kuyatii.

decisions.choice: everyone who comes ... he: the sentence starts with the subject and then begins again
decisions.reason: Jesus names the person first, then says what he will show about them.

decisions.choice: does them: obeys them
decisions.reason: Hearing and doing belong together (8:21; 11:28).

decisions.choice: Let me show you what someone is like who ...
alternatives: Everyone who ..., I will show you whom he is like
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main clause first, which reads more smoothly.

decisions.choice: the subject first, then a new start: "Todo el que viene ..., les mostraré a quién es semejante"
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with the subject and then starts again (meaning decision m1); Spanish can bear the break as English does. Balanced and Readable recast it, as the English does.

source.text: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν· πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: Like he is to a man building a house, who dug and deepened and laid a foundation on the rock; a flood then having come burst the river against the house that, and not was strong to shake it because of the well to have been built it.

en.L: {{gender:They are|He is}} like a {{gender:person|man}} building a house, who dug and deepened and laid a foundation on the rock; and when a flood came, the river burst against that house, and it was not strong enough to shake it, because it had been built well.
en.B: {{gender:That person is|He is}} like someone building a house, who dug, went down deep, and laid the foundation on the bedrock. When a flood came, the river crashed against that house but did not have the strength to shake it, because it had been built well.
en.R: That person is like someone who builds a house. The builder digs deep and puts the foundation on solid rock. When the river floods and the water rushes against the house, the water cannot even shake it, because it was built well.

es.L: Es semejante a {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} que edificaba una casa, quien cavó y ahondó y echó [los] cimientos sobre la roca; y cuando vino una inundación, el río se lanzó contra aquella casa, y no pudo sacudirla, porque había sido bien construida.
es.B: {{gender:Esa persona|Ese hombre}} es como alguien que, al construir una casa, cavó, ahondó y echó los cimientos sobre la roca firme. Cuando vino una inundación, el río embistió contra aquella casa, pero no tuvo fuerza para moverla, porque estaba bien construida.
es.R: Esa persona es como alguien que construye una casa. El constructor cava hondo y pone los cimientos sobre roca firme. Cuando el río crece y el agua golpea con fuerza contra la casa, el agua ni siquiera puede moverla, porque está bien construida.

sw.L: Anafanana na mtu ajengaye nyumba, aliyechimba na kwenda chini sana na kuweka msingi juu ya mwamba; na mafuriko yalipokuja, mto ukaipiga nyumba ile kwa nguvu, nao haukuweza kuitikisa, kwa sababu ilikuwa imejengwa vizuri.
sw.B: Mtu huyo ni kama mtu anayejenga nyumba, aliyechimba, akaenda chini sana, akaweka msingi juu ya mwamba. Mafuriko yalipokuja, mto ukaigonga nyumba ile kwa nguvu, lakini haukuweza kuitikisa, kwa sababu ilikuwa imejengwa vizuri.
sw.R: Mtu huyo ni kama mtu anayejenga nyumba. Mjenzi huyo anachimba chini sana na kuweka msingi juu ya mwamba imara. Mto unapofurika na maji yakaipiga nyumba ile kwa nguvu, maji hayawezi hata kuitikisa, kwa sababu ilijengwa vizuri.

decisions.choice: because it had been built well: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: for it had been founded on the rock, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "for it had been founded on the rock", the words of Matthew 7:25. Several early manuscripts have "because it had been built well". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a flood ... the river: a stream that rises suddenly in the rainy season
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel dry stream beds can fill in hours with winter rain and sweep away what stands in their path.

decisions.choice: the house that stands: a life built on hearing and doing Jesus's words, which stands when tested
decisions.reason: The flood pictures the testing that comes on every life, and finally God's judgment (compare Ezekiel 13:10-14).

decisions.choice: short sentences, with "the builder" as subject
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the parable and makes the subject of each step clear.

decisions.choice: the bedrock (B); solid rock (R)
decisions.reason: The article points to the rock beneath the soil.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.

records.literal_gloss: The one but having heard and not having done like is to a man having built a house on the ground without foundation, on which burst the river, and immediately it collapsed, and was the ruin of the house that great.

en.L: But the one who heard and did not do [them] is like a {{gender:person|man}} who built a house on the ground without a foundation, against which the river burst, and at once it collapsed, and the wreck of that house was great."
en.B: But whoever hears and does not act is like someone who built a house on the bare ground with no foundation. The river crashed against it, and at once it fell in, and that house was utterly destroyed."
en.R: But some people hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words and do not obey them. They are like someone who builds a house on the ground with no foundation. When the river rushes against it, the house falls down at once. It is completely destroyed!"

es.L: Pero el que oyó y no [las] hizo es semejante a {{gender:una persona|un hombre}} que edificó una casa sobre la tierra sin cimiento, contra la cual se lanzó el río, y enseguida se derrumbó, y la ruina de aquella casa fue grande».
es.B: Pero el que escucha y no actúa es como alguien que construyó una casa sobre el suelo desnudo, sin cimientos. El río embistió contra ella, y al instante se vino abajo, y aquella casa quedó totalmente destruida».
es.R: Pero hay personas que oyen {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} palabras y no las obedecen. Son como alguien que construye una casa sobre la tierra, sin cimientos. Cuando el río golpea contra ella, la casa se cae enseguida. ¡Queda completamente destruida!».

sw.L: Lakini yeye aliyesikia na hakuyatenda anafanana na mtu aliyejenga nyumba juu ya ardhi bila msingi, ambayo mto uliipiga kwa nguvu, na mara ikaanguka, na uharibifu wa nyumba ile ukawa mkubwa."
sw.B: Lakini mtu anayesikia na asitende ni kama mtu aliyejenga nyumba juu ya udongo mtupu bila msingi. Mto ulipoipiga kwa nguvu, mara ikaanguka, na nyumba ile ikaharibika kabisa."
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine husikia maneno {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wala hawayatii. Wao ni kama mtu anayejenga nyumba juu ya ardhi bila msingi. Mto unapoipiga kwa nguvu, nyumba ile huanguka mara moja. Inaharibika kabisa!"

decisions.choice: on the ground without a foundation: on the soil, with nothing dug beneath
decisions.reason: Luke's picture is a house set straight on the earth; Matthew 7:26 speaks of sand. The point is the same.

decisions.choice: the ruin of that house was great: total destruction
decisions.reason: The sermon ends on a warning: hearing without doing ends in disaster.

decisions.choice: my words
decisions.reason: Readable says what is heard, from 6:47.

decisions.choice: utterly destroyed (B); completely destroyed (R)
decisions.reason: Plain words for a great ruin.
